claim_text: Coagulation destabilizes particles or forms precipitates, while flocculation uses controlled contact to grow aggregates.
source_titles: Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Coagulation can involve charge neutralization, sweep coagulation, adsorption, bridging, or combinations; the chemical-versus-physical shorthand is incomplete.

claim_text: All clay, silt, algae, organic colour, bacteria, and precipitated metals are too small and electrically stable to ever settle, so gravity can never remove them.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: The listed materials span different particle sizes, densities, surface chemistries, and settling behaviour.

claim_text: Some fine and colloidal particles settle very slowly because of their size and stability, and coagulation-flocculation can improve their removal.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307; Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual
limitations: Settling behaviour remains water-specific and particle-specific.

claim_text: Under the United States Surface Water Treatment Rule, turbidity and log-removal credit is earned in coagulation rather than at the filter.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype; Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual
limitations: Filtered-water turbidity is a regulated performance measure and removal credit is associated with the treatment train, not coagulation alone.

claim_text: Under applicable United States Surface Water Treatment Rules, conventional and direct filtration systems must meet combined filter effluent turbidity limits of 0.3 NTU in at least 95 percent of measurements each month and 1 NTU as the maximum.
scope: Public water systems using conventional or direct filtration and covered by the applicable federal Surface Water Treatment Rule provisions.
source_titles: 40 CFR 141.173 Filtration; 40 CFR 141.551 Strengthened combined filter effluent turbidity limits; Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual
limitations: System size, rule subpart, filtration technology, monitoring, reporting, and state primacy requirements must be confirmed before use.

claim_text: One milligram per litre of alum fed produces about 0.26 milligrams per litre of sludge.
scope: Stoichiometric teaching factor shown on TDEC PDF page 10.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: This is not total plant sludge production; captured source-water solids, organics, other chemicals, product basis, and water content change actual residuals.

claim_text: Filtered-water turbidity is an operational indicator of treatment performance and potential pathogen-removal performance, not a direct measurement of pathogen concentration.
source_titles: Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual; Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual
limitations: It must not be described as a complete or visible proxy for pathogen protection.

claim_text: A clarifier carryover event will be named in a consent order.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Enforcement outcomes are jurisdiction-specific and fact-specific.

claim_text: Every raw-water particle has the same negative surface charge.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Surface charge varies by material and water chemistry.

claim_text: Many common colloids in natural waters carry negative surface charge, and metal coagulants can reduce repulsion under suitable chemical conditions.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307; Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual
limitations: Charge neutralization is one coagulation mechanism and does not explain every water or coagulant.

claim_text: Excess coagulant can cause charge reversal or restabilization under some water-specific conditions.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Requires an authoritative mechanism source; no universal dose threshold exists.

claim_text: Excessive mixing energy can break floc, and the balance between growth and breakage depends on water, coagulant, dose, time, and mixing conditions.
source_titles: Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual; Effects of velocity gradient and mixing time on particle growth in a rapid mixing tank; Influence of velocity gradient and rapid mixing time on flocs formed by polysilica iron and polyaluminum chloride
limitations: Study-specific breakage results cannot be converted into universal plant thresholds.

claim_text: Dose 88 and mixing energy 78 are technically meaningful thresholds for charge reversal and floc breakage.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: The values have no units, calibration, facility basis, or validated model.

claim_text: A colloid is universally defined as a nonsettling particle from 0.001 to 1 micrometre.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Size conventions vary, and settling is a rate and condition question rather than an absolute boundary.

claim_text: Raw water typically has zeta potential from minus 15 to minus 30 millivolts, and successful coagulation drives it toward zero.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: No authoritative supporting locator has been confirmed; optimum zeta potential is water-specific and mechanism-specific.

claim_text: Aluminum and iron coagulants can form hydrolysis products and precipitates that destabilize or capture particles through multiple mechanisms.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307; Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual
limitations: Species and dominant mechanisms vary with product and water chemistry.

claim_text: A polymer never replaces a primary coagulant and can only amplify it.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: TDEC page 11 states that some cationic polymers can serve as a primary coagulant or a coagulant aid.

claim_text: Polymers may act as primary coagulants, coagulant aids, flocculants, settling aids, filter aids, or sludge conditioners depending on product and application.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Product selection and dosing require supplier information, water testing, approved procedures, and qualified review.

claim_text: The conventional mean velocity-gradient parameter can be expressed as G equals the square root of power divided by dynamic viscosity and basin volume.
source_titles: Chemical Mixing, Nothing But a G Thing?; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Unit consistency, delivered power, nonuniform shear, basin geometry, and limitations of mean G must be taught.

claim_text: Tapered flocculation reduces mixing intensity through successive stages to support aggregate growth while limiting breakage.
source_titles: Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307; 12VAC5-590-871 Coagulation and flocculation
limitations: Exact staging and intensities are design-specific.

claim_text: Aluminum and iron salt coagulation can consume alkalinity and lower pH, affecting hydrolysis and treatment performance.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307; Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual
limitations: Effect depends on product basis, dose, starting alkalinity, pH, temperature, and water chemistry.

claim_text: A jar test is the only defensible way to set coagulant dose and is the record a regulator will request.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype; Long Term 2 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Toolbox Guidance Manual
limitations: Jar tests are important but may need filtration tests, pilot testing, full-scale confirmation, instrumentation, and jurisdiction-specific records.

claim_text: Jar testing can help compare coagulation conditions, but the test should represent source-water variation and the relevant full-scale processes and may need pilot or filterability confirmation.
source_titles: Long Term 2 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Toolbox Guidance Manual; Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual
limitations: A jar result is not automatic authorization for a plant change.

claim_text: Drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, reuse, and industrial treatment use identical coagulation-flocculation practice.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Mechanisms may overlap, but objectives, waters, regulations, equipment, residuals, and risk controls differ.

claim_text: Coagulation and flocculation performance influences clarification, solids loading, filtration, and residuals management downstream.
source_titles: Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual; Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual
limitations: Consequences depend on facility configuration and operating conditions.

claim_text: Reverse-osmosis fouling control is largely a coagulation problem solved upstream rather than at the membrane.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: RO fouling has multiple inorganic, organic, colloidal, and biological causes; pretreatment is system-specific.

claim_text: Conventional design universally uses rapid-mix G of 600 to 1000 per second for 30 to 60 seconds and flocculation G of 20 to 80 per second for 20 to 60 minutes.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype; 12VAC5-590-871 Coagulation and flocculation; Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual
limitations: Virginia provides state-specific typical rapid-mix combinations, while federal guidance and United States training references provide process context; none establishes one universal national operating range.

claim_text: Virginia requires the engineer to submit the basis for selected rapid-mix G considering chemicals and water temperature, and requires coagulant application at maximum mixing intensity.
source_titles: 12VAC5-590-871 Coagulation and flocculation
limitations: Applies in Virginia only and has no legal force in another state.

claim_text: United States federal guidance and state references describe flocculation after coagulation, gentle or tapered mixing, sufficient contact time, and controls intended to limit aggregate breakage.
scope: Federal process guidance with a separately labeled Virginia state design reference and Tennessee operator training context.
source_titles: Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual; Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual; 12VAC5-590-871 Coagulation and flocculation; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Federal guidance is not a universal design setpoint, and the state references apply only within their stated jurisdictions and purposes.

claim_text: In Park and colleagues' 2006 experiment, macrofloc counts at G 200 per second increased after 75 seconds, peaked at 150 seconds, and declined after 180 seconds.
scope: The specific experimental conditions in DOI 10.2166/wst.2006.212.
source_titles: Effects of velocity gradient and mixing time on particle growth in a rapid mixing tank
limitations: Not a general optimum and not transferable without reviewing the full methods and source water.

claim_text: In the Aktas study conditions, aggregation and breakup boundaries differed between polysilica iron and PACl, with maximum formation reported near G 546 and 390 per second respectively.
scope: The specific experimental conditions in DOI 10.1080/19443994.2012.751883.
source_titles: Influence of velocity gradient and rapid mixing time on flocs formed by polysilica iron and polyaluminum chloride
limitations: Study thresholds are not plant-wide limits and require full technical interpretation.

claim_text: A plant using PACl at rapid-mix G of 900 per second may be wasting energy and shearing floc, so a jar test and energy audit are indicated.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype; Influence of velocity gradient and rapid mixing time on flocs formed by polysilica iron and polyaluminum chloride
limitations: It extrapolates a study-specific threshold without plant hydraulics, water quality, dose, residence time, or delivered-power data.

claim_text: An alkalinity-based teaching reaction for hydrated aluminum sulfate can show bicarbonate consumption and aluminum-hydroxide precipitation.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Commercial product hydration and solution chemistry vary; a chemist must check species, balance, and notation.

claim_text: A bicarbonate-based teaching reaction for ferric chloride can show alkalinity consumption, ferric-hydroxide precipitation, chloride, and carbon dioxide.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Actual aqueous speciation and hydrolysis are more complex; a chemist must verify the equation and teaching boundary.

claim_text: Small microfloc or pin floc after coagulation can be an intended intermediate before further aggregation and separation.
source_titles: Long Term 1 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Provisions Technical Guidance Manual; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Appearance alone does not establish process success.

claim_text: Polyaluminum chloride and powdered activated carbon are different treatment chemicals, and the brief should use unambiguous abbreviations.
source_titles: Guidance for incorporation of water treatment effects on pesticide removal and transformation; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Local industry abbreviations vary; define PACl and PAC at first use.

claim_text: Polymer function cannot be assigned reliably from cationic, anionic, or nonionic charge class alone.
scope: Correction of the prototype's fixed polymer-role table.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: Molecular weight, charge density, water chemistry, process point, product instructions, and testing matter.

claim_text: Every jar test should use 100 to 300 rpm for 30 to 60 seconds, then 20 to 40 rpm, with polymer always added during flocculation.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype; Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: RPM is apparatus-specific, must be related to mixing conditions, and chemical sequence depends on the treatment program.

claim_text: Consistent settling time and sampling depth improve comparability among jar-test results.
source_titles: Coagulation and Flocculation Workshop, Course 307
limitations: A complete reviewed SOP must specify apparatus, mixing calibration, dosing, replication, analytical methods, and decision criteria.

claim_text: Coagulant dose should be reassessed when meaningful source-water or treatment conditions change rather than held fixed solely by habit.
source_titles: Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual; Long Term 2 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Toolbox Guidance Manual
limitations: Reassessment does not authorize an unapproved dose change.

claim_text: Written, approved procedures should govern chemical changes and define the evidence, authority, limits, monitoring, and rollback conditions.
source_titles: Long Term 2 Enhanced Surface Water Treatment Rule Toolbox Guidance Manual
limitations: Procedure content and sign-off roles are facility-specific and jurisdiction-specific.

claim_text: Streaming-current measurement is a direct real-time substitute for zeta-potential measurement.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Related electrokinetic signals are not interchangeable; instrument response and control use need a dedicated source and practitioner review.

claim_text: Dose, raw and settled turbidity, pH, alkalinity, and relevant process signals should be available as one time-aligned, queryable dataset.
scope: OWOS data and Graph product direction.
limitations: Signal selection, semantics, security, quality controls, and facility architecture require design review.

claim_text: Storm response and land-use data can predict coagulant dose before a storm reaches a plant.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Requires site data, model validation, uncertainty bounds, monitoring, and human decision authority.

claim_text: Chemical optimization always produces operating savings without capital investment and is defensible in a rate case.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Optimization may require testing, instrumentation, controls, training, engineering, residuals changes, and jurisdiction-specific rate evidence.

claim_text: A single concept brief can provide different evidence-bounded next actions for operators, engineers, utility leaders, regulators, data teams, and finance teams.
limitations: Actions require representative-user and role-authority review.

claim_text: Every published number and material assertion in the brief will expose its evidence class, exact source locator, scope, and review status.
limitations: This is a release requirement, not a statement that the current working prototype already satisfies it.

claim_text: The working pilot has complete supplied-claim inventory but incomplete independent and qualified review, so it must not be used as site-specific operating, engineering, or regulatory guidance.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Update after each review gate.

claim_text: The working brief does not authorize a facility dose, mixing, chemical, or process change.
source_titles: Coagulation vs Flocculation Concept Brief prototype
limitations: Final wording requires legal, technical, and editorial review.
